bilingual.notes: Bilingual Authorization (CL-628B) is the current new-issue add-on pathway (AB 1871, 2008); BCLAD/Bilingual Crosscultural Specialist Credential lineage is the standalone form. Pathways: (1) Commission-approved bilingual program; (2) CSET World Languages Tests II/III, IV, V; (3) program + CSET equivalency. Practicum not separately enumerated in leaflet — coded null.

eld.notes: EL Authorization / CLAD Certificate (CL-628C) plus embedded EL preparation in every Multiple/Single Subject preliminary credential issued since 7/1/2002 (AB 1059). Pathways include CTEL Examination, approved CTEL program, program+exam equivalency, legacy ESL/SDAIE, SB 1969/CCSD, NBPTS ENL, out-of-state equivalency. Second-language requirement waived for candidates with a bachelor's degree from a regionally-accredited institution.

sei.notes: California's SEI-equivalent mandate is the AB 1059 embedded EL authorization in every Multiple Subject and Single Subject preliminary credential issued since 7/1/2002 — functionally one-course-plus EL preparation required of every newly-credentialed classroom teacher.

history.title: Chacón-Moscone Bilingual-Bicultural Education Act enacted (AB 1329, Stats. 1976 ch. 978)
history.description: California's first comprehensive bilingual-education statute required districts to provide bilingual instruction wherever 10 or more EL students of the same primary language were enrolled in the same grade at a school. The act underwrote two decades of growth in California bilingual programs and bilingual-teacher credentialing infrastructure (the BCLAD pathway descends from it). The legislature allowed Chacón-Moscone to sunset in 1987, but the State Board of Education continued most of its requirements administratively until Proposition 227 (1998) overrode them.

history.title: Voters approve Proposition 227 — English-only mandate (English in Public Schools Initiative)
history.description: Funded by Ron Unz, Prop 227 passed roughly 61%–39% and rewrote California Education Code §§300-340 to require Sheltered English Immersion for nearly all EL students, capping it at "normally not to exceed one year" and narrowing parental waivers. Bilingual programs collapsed statewide and the BCLAD credential pipeline contracted sharply. Prop 227 remained in force until voters approved Proposition 58 in 2016, which restored district choice. The Unz model exported to Arizona (Prop 203, 2000) and Massachusetts (Question 2, 2002).

history.title: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.

history.title: AB 1059 EL preparation embedded in every preliminary credential
history.description: Effective 2002-07-01 (AB 1059, 1999), every Multiple Subject and Single Subject preliminary teaching credential issued by California must embed EL preparation, making CA's universal EL-credentialing mandate functionally one-course-plus EL preparation required of every newly-credentialed classroom teacher.

history.title: AB 1871 establishes current Bilingual Authorization (CL-628B)
history.description: AB 1871 (2008) restructured California's bilingual credentialing into the current Bilingual Authorization issued under CL-628B. Pathways: a Commission-approved bilingual program, CSET World Languages Tests II/III + IV + V, or program + CSET equivalency. Successor to the BCLAD/Bilingual Crosscultural Specialist Credential lineage.

history.title: California State Seal of Biliteracy enacted (AB 815)
history.description: Governor signed AB 815 establishing the California State Seal of Biliteracy — the nation's first state-level Seal — recognizing high school graduates who attain proficiency in English and one or more world languages.

history.title: Voters approve Proposition 58 (CA Ed.G.E. Act)
history.description: Proposition 58 (the California Education for a Global Economy Initiative) repeals the English-only instruction restrictions of Proposition 227 (1998), restoring local authority to offer bilingual, dual-language, and structured English immersion programs and reinforcing demand for the Bilingual Authorization.

history.title: CTC adopts revised California Standards for the Teaching Profession (CSTP)
history.description: CTC adopted the April 2024 revision of the California Standards for the Teaching Profession; standards continue to reference EL/cultural/linguistic diversity explicitly and bind all California teachers.
